_comment: uv.lock carries a self-referential `[[package]]` entry for this project,
and release-please bumping pyproject.toml WITHOUT it left the lock
PERMANENTLY one release behind (livespec-runtime-jis). The first `uv`
invocation in any fresh clone or worktree then regenerated the lock and
left the tree dirty with a one-line restatement nobody authored — three
times in a single day (0.22.1, 0.22.2, 0.22.3) — which every session had
to notice, attribute and route around, and which is trivially swept into
an unrelated PR by a reflexive `git add -A`.
THE `.name.value` IN THE FILTER IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT A TYPO.
release-please's toml updater parses with a position-tracking parser that
wraps every scalar as {start, end, value}, so `@.name` is an OBJECT and
`@.name=='livespec-runtime'` never matches. The obvious-looking
`$.package[?(@.name=='livespec-runtime')].version` was tested against this
exact file and SILENTLY MATCHED NOTHING: release-please logs
'No entries modified' at warn level and returns the content unchanged, so
a wrong path here reports success while doing nothing.
Verified by running release-please 17.11.2's GenericToml updater against
this repo's real uv.lock before this landed: exactly ONE line changes, the
one directly under `name = "livespec-runtime"`, with the line count
unchanged even for a different-length version. The naive `@.name==` form
was run through the same probe and changed nothing. If you edit this
entry, re-run that check — the failure mode is silence, not an error.
This mirrors livespec-overseer's config, which has carried the identical
typed-toml entry (not a `generic` one — uv.lock has no place to anchor an
`x-release-please-version` marker) across its last 25 releases with
pyproject.toml and uv.lock in lockstep.
